notes.title: 1.1.108 Release Notes!
notes.notes:
Today we're pushing the latest and greatest update for Freedom Finger. Most of our changes are under the hood, aimed at improving performance and fixing bugs. Check out the patch notes below.

As always, if we missed something, [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/1005410/discussions/1/]head on over to the bug discussion board and let us know![/url]


[b]Quality of Life[/b]
Added Japanese and Traditional Chinese translations (translations courtesy of EastAsiaSoft).
Achievements have been localized. (Steam)
For players with older GPUs, we've added an option in the Video Settings to remove shaders on level 5-3. (Steam)

[b]Graphics and UI[/b]
Fixed error with embolden Chinese/Japanese font.
KOWP flower was not indicating damage properly.
Added the Travis font to all menus.
MIR space station was layered incorrectly.
Arcade Mode renamed to Arcade. It's cleaner.
Adjusted version number on splash screen. (Steam)

[b]Bugs[/b]
Battledome top and bottom boundaries were not wide enough.
Fixed chapter select title bar glitch.
Certain enemies kept moving during the pause/share menu. (PS4/Xbox)
Level 6-1: Grabbing the Chinese Heli enemy now disables its shields automatically. 
Level 7-1: Sauce Cap cannons projectiles have been repositioned. 
Fixed crash during Battledome cutscene. 
Fixed crash if tutorial cinematics were skipped too quickly. 

[b]Misc.[/b]
Security update. (Steam)
Updated Credits.

notes.title: The Rhymesayers Update - NOW AVAILABLE!
notes.notes:
[previewyoutube=YKQ-r0vPpz8;full][/previewyoutube]

The Rhymesayers Update, a FREE content update for Freedom Finger, is AVAILABLE NOW!.

This exciting new update adds new levels featuring original music by legendary underground hip-hop artist, Aesop Rock.  Additionally, the update features a wide variety of enhancements and fixes:

[b][u]Gameplay [/u]
New price: $14.99 (cheap!) 
Save slots added to Campaign mode. Players can now have three active campaigns.
All levels are automatically unlocked in Arcade mode.
Altered Tipper Gore achievement (easier to complete).
Level 5-3: Missile Launcher dong projectiles are now punchable.
Level 12: Fixed layering issue with player's trails.
Level 5-Boss: Fixed audio looping error.

[u]Accessibility[/u]
Subtitles now available in German and Spanish.
Updated Chinese and Russian translation.
Added high contrast text selection option.
Added subtitles for audio specific cutscenes.
Updated audio sliders. Players now have greater control over SFX, Music, and Voice volume.

[u]Difficulty[/u]
Rebalanced one-hit HP point modifier. 
400% and Infinite health options added. 

[u]Extras[/u]
Added new political quotes and hints to loading screen.
Level 5-1: Fixed Germ Baby's vibration bug.
Censoring Subtitles now prevents quotes with cursing from appearing during loading screens.
In-game Achievements are now translated.
Fixed various subtitle errors. 
Updated Credits.[/b]

For more info, follow Wide Right Interactive on [url=twitter.com/widerightgames]Twitter[/url]. or visit [url=WideRightGames.com]WideRightGames.com[/url].

Now, to the casual outsider, what we’re doing might seem absolutely nuts, but we thought we’d put together an alphabetical list of all the PC games that have been confirmed to appear at this year’s E3 show. notes.title: Freedom Finger is a hand-drawn shoot 'em up with a stellar cast
notes.notes:
Freedom Finger is a space shoot 'em up where you pilot an angry fist as it tears across the galaxy. It's trying pretty hard to be 'crazy', but also promises a great cast of voice actors, including Nolan North and John DiMaggio, and a soundtrack full of licensed music from the likes of Red Fang, METZ and Power Trip. Watch the trailer above.

As rookie pilot Gamma Ray—probably not the last pun—you'll set out to save a bunch of scientists with your fist-shaped ship, determining their fate and uncovering something more sinister. Mostly, though, you'll be blowing shit up across 36 levels.

The fist isn't just an aesthetic choice. It can beat enemies up in melee combat, punching, grabbing and tossing them around, and when it flips the bird, it fires bullets. You can enhance it with power-ups, and the trailer shows off a few different projectiles. 

The soundtrack's a big deal. Attack patterns, enemies and level events all sync up to the music, so as well as being a shmup, it's a bit like a rhythm action game. It's is full of tracks from bands I've never heard of, but only because I listen to the same Spotify playlist over and over and fear change. You can see a list of them on the Steam page.

Freedom Finger is due out this year.
